instruction: Determine how many students are in each of the following categories: Fail, Pass, Average, Above average, Excellent, Exceptional!, and write these counts in cells H2 to H7.

metadata.explanation: Task requires counting students in each grade category and writing counts to specified cells. Verified with Python script: Fail=3 (Arnold 6, Tom 10, Kanye 5), Pass=4 (Benedict 42, Bey 33, Parah 59, 50 Dollar 32), Average=3 (Olivia 67, Elijah 60, Reese 73), Above average=2 (Clint 86, John 85), Excellent=1 (Blake 94), Exceptional!=1 (Swan 100). Custom getter reads counts from cells H2-H7, custom metric validates all 6 counts.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts category counts from the exact cells specified in instruction (H2-H7 for 6 categories)
Metric correctly compares all 6 category counts with proper partial credit scoring (correct_count / total_categories)
Expected values are semantically correct and verified against actual student data (Fail=3, Pass=4, Average=3, Above average=2, Excellent=1, Exceptional!=1)
Complete coverage of all instruction requirements - all 6 categories are verified
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) to ensure state persistence before verification
Edge cases properly handled: None values default to 0, non-numeric data caught with try/except, missing files return empty dict
Data flow is logically sound: postconfig saves file -> getter reads persisted counts from cells -> metric compares against expected
Metric parameter handling is correct: 'expected' parameter directly receives rules dict (expected.get('category_counts')) without incorrect nesting
